The grey espresso machine at the counter's far end still reads as the first thing noticed on a glance, just by a smaller margin (+0.078 measured focal contrast vs +0.166). Recorded as honest secondary evidence, not cherry-picked.

The service counter (espresso machine, back wall, framed between two windows and the chalkboard signage above it) reads as the room's focal point on a first glance: it sits on the only large light-toned surface break against the darker floor, at the architecturally privileged back-wall position, with real contrast margin over the rest of the frame (+0.048 mean L, +0.167 contrast, +0.054 detail vs elsewhere, all measured). Genuine competition exists that the cozy_ghibli reference doesn't have to the same degree -- snes_rpg's higher saturation makes the bright green rug (with a solid-green-clothed customer standing on it) and the magenta/pink bench and cafe-table set noticeably more eye-catching than their more desaturated cozy_ghibli counterparts, and a viewer's eye plausibly visits those patches too. But on a sub-second glance the counter is still what I'd name first: it's the only element combining position (back wall, elevated), framing (windows + chalkboard bracket it), and a clean value break, where the coloured patches are saturation-driven pulls without that same structural backing. Closer call than cozy_ghibli's version of this room, worth someone re-checking by eye if the palette gets more saturated still.
